title: Listening Comprehension
intro: Listen to a dialogue, then answer multiple choice questions. These are generated review dialogues on Module 1 topics, because the quiz dialogue is only played in class.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Leo, why does your robot keep making that popping noise?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: The motor sputters every time I turn it on. My first design was a complete flop.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Don't give up. Thomas Edison tested thousands of ideas before his incandescent bulb worked.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: That's true. I will build a new prototype with a bigger battery this weekend.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: If it works, you should apply for a patent so nobody can copy your gadget.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Good idea. First I need it to run for more than ten seconds!

questions.q: What problem does Leo's robot have?
choices: The motor sputters and makes popping noises.
It is painted the wrong color.
It is too heavy to carry.

questions.q: What does Leo call his first design?
Why does Ava mention Thomas Edison?
choices: To tell Leo about a train
To encourage Leo not to give up
To ask Leo for a light bulb
To say robots are a bad idea

questions.q: What will Leo do this weekend?
choices: Build a new prototype with a bigger battery
Sell his robot at the market

questions.q: Why does Ava think Leo should get a patent?
choices: So he can win a prize
So nobody can copy his gadget

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: Molly, I heard you want to start a recycling club at school.

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: Yes! My objective is to cut the trash in our cafeteria in half by December.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: That is a big goal. How will you begin?

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: First, I will put labeled bins next to every trash can. Then I will give a short talk in the auditorium to explain what goes where.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: You are evidently very passionate about this. I can help you order the bins.

lines.speaker: Molly
lines.text: Thank you! Every small contribution makes a difference.

questions.q: What does Molly want to start?
What is Molly's objective?
choices: To cut the cafeteria trash in half by December
To buy a new trash can
To give a speech every day

questions.q: What will Molly do first?
choices: Give a talk in the auditorium
Put labeled bins next to every trash can

questions.q: Where will Molly give her short talk?
How will Mr. Chen help?
choices: He will help order the bins.
He will give the talk for her.
He will collect the cans himself.

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: Welcome to tryouts, Sam. Have you played wheelchair basketball before?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Only with my cousin. He can maneuver his chair around anyone.

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: Speed and quick acceleration matter, but passing matters more. Let's see you pass to Jordan.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Okay. Should I push forward while I pass?

lines.speaker: Coach Rivera
lines.text: Yes. Keep your eyes up, not on the wheels. Nice! You have good control.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thanks. My impulse was to look down, but I remembered what you said.

questions.q: Where does this conversation take place?
Who has Sam played with before?
According to the coach, what matters most?
What does the coach tell Sam to do with his eyes?
choices: Keep them up, not on the wheels

questions.q: What was Sam's impulse?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Did you finish reading about William and the windmill?

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: Yes. His village was impoverished, and there was no rain, so the crops died.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He found a picture of a windmill in a library book and built one from junk parts, like an old bicycle.

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: People said he was eccentric, but the windmill made electricity for his house.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Later he built a bigger one that pumped water to irrigate the fields.

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: That is why the story is called Winds of Hope. One idea changed the whole village.

questions.q: What problem did William's village have?
choices: It was impoverished and there was no rain, so crops died.

questions.q: Where did William find the idea for the windmill?
What did William use to build the windmill?
choices: Junk parts, like an old bicycle

questions.q: What did the first windmill do?
What did the bigger windmill do?
choices: Pumped water to irrigate the fields
